beats.say: This tiny light is far more efficient than a bulb, but connect it the wrong way and it won't light at all.
An LED has two legs. The longer leg is the anode, positive. The shorter leg is the cathode, negative.
Its symbol is a diode with two arrows, for the light coming out. Current flows the way the triangle points.
Always add a resistor in series, or the LED draws too much current and burns out.
To pick the resistor, take the supply voltage, subtract the LED's voltage, and divide by the current you want.
Next time: the diode. Subscribe so you don't miss it.
